_readme: PlanRouter config. Pure stdlib, Python 3.10+, no runtime dependencies. Run: pip install -e . && planrouter --config router.example.json --check ; then planrouter --config router.example.json . Point your coding agent at http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1 (OpenAI) or /v1/messages (Anthropic) with listen.api_key as the bearer token. Secrets use env:VAR so nothing lands in this file or in logs. A channel is any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint: a direct API key, a free tier, or a local bridge (one-api / new-api / CLIProxyAPI) that exposes a coding-plan subscription. Protocols are NEVER converted: /v1/chat/completions only reaches openai channels, /v1/messages only reaches anthropic channels. If a plan speaks a different protocol, put a bridge in front of it. On 429 / quota errors the channel is cooled for the upstream reset time (Retry-After, *-reset headers) or cooldown_minutes (default 300 = 5h, matching typical plan windows); the next healthy channel serves the request automatically. Transient 5xx/network errors cool for 30s with a half-open probe. Add X-Session-Id (or body.user) for 30-minute session stickiness so prefix caches survive; X-Route: cheap or model=auto:cheap selects a cheaper chain. Responses carry X-Routed-Via and X-Failover-Count. MODEL NAMES: point tools at our own id facet-auto (also facet-cheap, or any id under models.branded) instead of auto; any other model name is first matched against the explicit models keys of the channels in the selected route, and when it does not match, the router schedules internally using each channel's auto mapping. Set models.fallback_unknown=false to reject unknown names instead. Responses carry X-Routed-Model-Mode (auto|exact|fallback), X-Routed-Model-Reason, X-Routed-Requested-Model and X-Route. GET /health shows remaining cooldowns, GET /stats shows per-channel usage. Observability: every forward attempt is appended to requests.jsonl (routing metadata only, never prompts, keys or outputs; --audit-file moves it) and readable via GET /api/requests or the console's Recent requests table; streaming token usage is collected from upstream usage chunks when defaults.track_stream_usage is true (set it false if an upstream rejects stream_options). POST /v1/messages/count_tokens is answered locally with a heuristic estimate (X-Token-Estimate: local-heuristic) so Claude Code does not 404. Security: set listen.admin_key to a separate secret for /api/* (the console prompts for it) and cross-site POSTs are rejected; without it the management API falls back to listen.api_key. Codex CLI: POST /v1/responses is bridged to the chat channels, so a custom model provider can keep wire_api='responses' with base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1 and the model field set to facet-auto. The bridge maps instructions, input items (message/function_call/function_call_output/reasoning), tools and tool_choice to chat messages, and emits Responses SSE events (response.output_text.delta, response.output_item.added/done, response.completed). Limits: non-function tools such as web_search are dropped, reasoning items are flattened to text, previous_response_id and /v1/responses/compact are unsupported, and streamed tool calls are emitted as complete items at the end of the stream; use wire_api='chat' for full fidelity. Channel URLs: base_url is the API root; the gateway appends /v1/chat/completions (or /v1/messages) unless upstream_path is set. If base_url already contains a version segment (e.g. /api/v1 or /api/paas/v4), set upstream_path='/chat/completions' to avoid a duplicated /v1; --check warns about this. Quota prediction: when an upstream reports remaining/limit/reset headers (OpenAI x-ratelimit-* or Anthropic anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*), the router records the window in /health, /stats and the console; if a remaining count is 0 it cools that channel ahead of the 429 using the reset time (defaults.preempt_quota, true by default; without a reset header only a short backoff is used). Subscription quota fields and the monthly report live in subscriptions.json / GET /api/report/YYYY-MM. Model catalog: the console's 拉取模型 button fetches a channel's upstream /models list with its key (POST /api/probe/models), records it (fetched_at, endpoint, diff vs previous) and the whole catalog is refreshed automatically every defaults.catalog_refresh_hours (24h default, 0 disables); the catalog is a known list used for soft validation — when it provably lacks the requested model on a channel, that channel is skipped, while unknown names are still passed through and marked model_unverified in requests.jsonl. AUTO-MAINTENANCE: every defaults.maintenance_hours the router re-probes each channel's catalog and applies only catalog-confirmed changes itself (de-listed model mappings are removed and a broken auto mapping is re-pointed to the closest surviving model; the config is backed up to <config>.maintenance.bak first). New-model and rate-limit suggestions wait in the console's 自动运维 card for one-click adoption, and invalid keys are reported only. Set defaults.maintenance_model to any model this gateway serves to add an LLM review pass on top of the deterministic rules — the router calls itself over loopback, so pick a model your free quotas cover; reports are kept in memory (last 20) and appended to maintenance.jsonl next to the config. For personal use with credentials you are entitled to; each provider's terms still apply.
